 Building A 7%-Yielding Dividend Growth Portfolio With SCHD As Its Core Holding
 Oct 29, 2026, 7:05 AM ET SCHD , VYM , VIG , DGRO , PG , KO , CVX , MRK , UNH , TXN , QCOM , XLK , PAVE , VNQ , BIZD , GPIQ , QQQI , QYLD , JEPQ , O , NNN , WPC , MAIN , TRIN , AMLP , HESM , MPLX , WES , UTF , GLD , PFF , BKLN , PG:CA , COLA:CA , CVX:CA , ZCVX:CA , MRK:CA , UNH:CA , ZUNH:CA , QCOM:CA 25 Comments 4 Likes Samuel Smith Investing Group Follow Summary
 SCHD is one of the best dividend growth ETFs available, but its modest 3% yield and several important diversification gaps make it insufficient for many income-focused retirees.
 I explain how investors can potentially more than double SCHD's yield while maintaining meaningful dividend growth, broad diversification, and exposure to several beaten-down high-yield sectors.
 I share a near-7%-yielding retirement portfolio blueprint, including specific holdings, portfolio allocations, and the key risks investors should understand before putting their retirement savings to work.
